instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Different types of images are stored differently by computers. The easiest type of image to store is a black and white image.

atoms.a: What colours can a pixel have in a black and white image?
How many different colour values can a pixel in a black and white image have?

instruction.text: For an image to be encoded as black and white, all pixels must be either black or white. Select all truly black and white images.

trainers.hint: An image cannot be encoded as black and white if it has any bright colours or even shades of grey.

feedback.finish: When we encode a black and white image, we give the binary value 0 to black pixels and the value 1 to white pixels.

trainers.hint: The grey lines are for orientation purposes only. They are not part of the black and white image.

instruction.text: Select all pixels in this black and white image that are encoded with the value 0.

To encode an image, we "read" the pixels one by one from left to right and top to bottom. Encode each pixel to get the image code piece by piece.

Black: 0      White: 1
instruction.sound: To encode an image, we reed the pixels one by one, from left to right and top to bottom. Encode each pixel to get the image code piece by piece.

instruction.text: Has the image been successfully encoded?
